# Data Source: stripe_refund

A refund of a charge or payment intent. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_refund" "order" {
  id = "re_123"
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the refund to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - Amount, in cents (or local equivalent).
* `balance_transaction` - Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.
* `charge` - ID of the charge that's refunded.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - ID of the customer of this refund.
* `customer_account` - ID of the account of this refund.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. You can use this for displaying to users (available on non-card refunds only).
* `destination_details` - See [`destination_details`](#destination_details) below.
* `failure_balance_transaction` - After the refund fails, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.
* `failure_reason` - Provides the reason for the refund failure. Possible values are: `lost_or_stolen_card`, `expired_or_canceled_card`, `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed`, `insufficient_funds`, `declined`, `merchant_request`, or `unknown`.
* `instructions_email` - For payment methods without native refund support (for example, Konbini, PromptPay), provide an email address for the customer to receive refund instructions.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `next_action` - See [`next_action`](#next_action) below.
* `payment_intent` - ID of the PaymentIntent that's refunded.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method associated with this refund.
* `pending_reason` - Provides the reason for why the refund is pending. Possible values are: `processing`, `insufficient_funds`, or `charge_pending`. Possible values: `charge_pending`, `insufficient_funds`, `processing`.
* `presentment_details` - See [`presentment_details`](#presentment_details) below.
* `reason` - Reason for the refund, which is either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, or `requested_by_customer`) or generated by Stripe internally (`expired_uncaptured_charge`). Possible values: `duplicate`, `expired_uncaptured_charge`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`.
* `receipt_number` - This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.
* `source_transfer_reversal` - The transfer reversal that's associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account.
* `status` - Status of the refund. This can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`. Learn more about [failed refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds#failed-refunds).
* `transfer_reversal` - This refers to the transfer reversal object if the accompanying transfer reverses. This is only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.

<a id="destination_details"></a>
### `destination_details`

The `destination_details` attribute supports:

* `blik` - See [`destination_details.blik`](#destination_details.blik) below.
* `br_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.br_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.br_bank_transfer) below.
* `card` - See [`destination_details.card`](#destination_details.card) below.
* `crypto` - See [`destination_details.crypto`](#destination_details.crypto) below.
* `eu_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.eu_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.eu_bank_transfer) below.
* `gb_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.gb_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.gb_bank_transfer) below.
* `jp_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.jp_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.jp_bank_transfer) below.
* `mb_way` - See [`destination_details.mb_way`](#destination_details.mb_way) below.
* `multibanco` - See [`destination_details.multibanco`](#destination_details.multibanco) below.
* `mx_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.mx_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.mx_bank_transfer) below.
* `p24` - See [`destination_details.p24`](#destination_details.p24) below.
* `paypal` - See [`destination_details.paypal`](#destination_details.paypal) below.
* `swish` - See [`destination_details.swish`](#destination_details.swish) below.
* `th_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.th_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.th_bank_transfer) below.
* `type` - The type of transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the refund (e.g., `card`). An additional hash is included on `destination_details` with a name matching this value. It contains information specific to the refund transaction.
* `us_bank_transfer` - See [`destination_details.us_bank_transfer`](#destination_details.us_bank_transfer) below.

<a id="destination_details.blik"></a>
### `destination_details.blik`

The `destination_details.blik` attribute supports:

* `network_decline_code` - For refunds declined by the network, a decline code provided by the network which indicates the reason the refund failed.
* `reference` - The reference assigned to the refund.
* `reference_status` - Status of the reference on the refund. This can be `pending`, `available` or `unavailable`.

<a id="destination_details.card"></a>
### `destination_details.card`

The `destination_details.card` attribute supports:

* `reference` - Value of the reference number assigned to the refund.
* `reference_status` - Status of the reference number on the refund. This can be `pending`, `available` or `unavailable`.
* `reference_type` - Type of the reference number assigned to the refund.
* `type` - The type of refund. This can be `refund`, `reversal`, or `pending`. Possible values: `pending`, `refund`, `reversal`.
